content.content: A journal entry is `{id, version, kind, target, before, after}`: `before` and `after` map an owned path to a 64-hex content hash or null for absent. The id is the SHA-256 of the canonical entry; blob paths are SHA-256 content-addressed, so identical content dedupes. Blobs are written before the entry, and the entry lands temp-then-rename. A corrupt entry refuses naming it; unreferenced entries and blobs are removable.
content.rationale: An id derived from the entry makes the entry self-checking: a reader recomputes it and refuses a document that does not match its name. Content addressing dedupes unchanged files across recordings and makes a blob immutable. Writing blobs first and the entry last means a visible entry always has every blob it names, and atomic replacement keeps a crash from leaving half an entry. Garbage collection is a scan of the marker file, not a reachability protocol.
